EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN NOTE (outside facility, central Florida)
Date of visit: 01/10/2026. Received by fax 01/14/2026.

CC: lightheaded and dizzy during a marathon.

HPI: 33-year-old woman running a marathon this morning in warm, humid weather. Reports she took no fluids from the start. Around mile 10 became lightheaded and dizzy, slowed down and stopped to rest for a few minutes; noticed a dry mouth and that her skin felt sticky. Has not voided since the start of the race. Race medical tent noted HR 104 and BP 98/66, with weight 3 lb under her pre-race check-in weight, and sent her in for evaluation. Denies any recent illness, vomiting or diarrhea. No chest pain, no syncope, no headache, no confusion.

PMH: cryptosporidium infection, summer 2025, resolved.
PSH: tonsillectomy, wisdom teeth extraction.
Medications: none.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family hx: mother hypothyroidism, father hypertension.
Social: never smoker, social alcohol, works in international business development.

Exam on arrival: T 37.3, HR 98, BP 102/68, RR 18, SpO2 99% RA. Alert, oriented, conversant. Mucous membranes dry. Lungs clear. Heart regular, mildly tachycardic, no murmur. Abdomen benign. No focal neuro deficit. Skin warm.

Labs: BMP within reference range, sodium normal.

ED course: 1 L normal saline IV. Encouraged oral fluids, tolerated well. Repeat HR 78, BP 114/72. Ambulating without dizziness.

Impression: volume depletion / dehydration from exertion in heat without fluid intake.

Disposition: discharged in stable condition. Oral fluids with electrolytes for the next 24 hours, rest, no running for several days. Follow up with primary care in 1 week. Return for fainting, confusion, chest pain, or inability to keep fluids down.

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD (hospital at cruise port of call)
Visit 07/20/2026. Copy received 07/24/2026 at patient request.

Chief complaint: vomiting and diarrhea x 24 h.

History: 33 y/o female passenger on a cruise. Sudden onset yesterday of severe nausea, then repeated vomiting and frequent watery, nonbloody diarrhea. Cannot keep down food or liquids. Many other passengers on the ship sick with the same illness. Husband, who ate every meal with her, became ill with the same symptoms a few hours before she did. No raw shellfish, no undercooked meat, no unpasteurized dairy. Nobody in their group with fever or blood in the stool.

Past history: cryptosporidiosis 2025; dehydration after a marathon 01/2026, recovered. Surgeries: tonsillectomy, wisdom teeth.
Medications: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Social: never smoker, occasional alcohol.

Triage: T 37.1 C, HR 106, BP 110/70, RR 16, SpO2 99%.
Exam: Tired-appearing but alert and oriented x3. Dry mucous membranes. Mild tachycardia, regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nondistended, without peritoneal signs. No rash.

Stool: fecal leukocytes negative; ova and parasite exam negative.

Treatment: NS 1 L IV bolus; ondansetron 4 mg IV. Nausea settled; drank oral fluids without vomiting. HR 88 on recheck.

Assessment: acute gastroenteritis in a shipboard outbreak, most consistent with norovirus. Dehydration.

Disposition: discharged back to ship, stable. Rx ondansetron 4 mg ODT q8h PRN nausea, #6. Small frequent sips of oral rehydration fluid, strict handwashing (alcohol gel does not reliably kill this virus), stay in cabin until 48 h symptom-free. Return for blood in stool, high fever, confusion, or inability to keep fluids down. See primary doctor after returning home.
